slides.title: Part 1 — Assembling the whole thing
slides.body: You have every component. A transformer block is just the right wiring of them — and it stacks.

slides.title: The block (pre-norm)
slides.body:
One block, modern pre-norm form:

```
h = x + MultiHeadAttn(LayerNorm(x))   # mix across tokens
y = h + FFN(LayerNorm(h))            # transform per token
```

Two sublayers, each wrapped in its own LayerNorm (inside) and residual (around). In/out width is $d_{model}$ both times, so blocks are *composable* — stack $N$ of them and nothing else changes.

slides.title: Attention mixes tokens, FFN mixes features
slides.body: The division of labor, crisply: **attention** is the only cross-token operation (routing/aggregating information between positions); the **FFN** is the only per-token nonlinear transform (computing on each position independently); **LayerNorm + residual** are the stabilizers that let you stack the pair dozens of times. Every modern LLM is essentially this block repeated.

question.question: Order of operations for the attention sublayer in a PRE-norm block?
options: save residual → LayerNorm → attention → add to residual
question.explanation: Pre-norm applies LN to the *input* before attention; attention's output is then added to the saved residual. The residual stream itself is never directly normalized — only the sublayer inputs are.

question.question: Order one pre-norm attention sublayer's steps, first to last.

items.label: Add result back to the saved residual

question.explanation: Pre-norm sublayer: residual = x → x = LN(x) → x = Attention(x) → x = residual + x. The same shape repeats for the FFN sublayer. A whole transformer is just this pattern, twice per block, N blocks deep.

question.question: Assemble a pre-norm transformer block
question.goal: From: stack attention + FFN so depth trains stably.

steps.motivation: Norm *inside* each sublayer and an identity residual *around* it keeps the gradient path clean as depth grows.

options: h = x + Attn(LN(x)); out = h + FFN(LN(h))
One LayerNorm at the very end

hints: Residual wraps each sublayer; LN sits inside it (pre-norm).
steps.reveal: h = x + Attn(LN(x)); out = h + FFN(LN(h)) — residual around each, norm inside.

steps.prompt: Why does the residual stream let you stack many blocks?
steps.motivation: The identity path carries gradient undiminished; each block only learns a delta on top of it.

rubricCriteria.description: the identity/residual path carries gradient without vanishing
each block adds a learned delta to the stream
so depth can grow without the signal degrading

hints: Think about the gradient through x + f(x).
steps.reveal: x + f(x) has gradient 1 + f'(x): the +1 keeps gradient flowing, so blocks compose to great depth.

question.question: Turn the residual off and stack depth — watch the gradient-norm proxy collapse; with residual on it survives (target ≥ 0.1).
question.explanation: Without residual the per-block factor (<1) multiplies to ~0 over depth — vanishing gradient. The residual identity (factor 1) keeps it alive.

slides.title: How big is big?
slides.body: GPT-3: 96 blocks, $d_{model}=12288$, 96 heads, $d_{ff}=4d_{model}$ → 175B params. The block didn't change — it was *scaled and repeated*. Scaling laws say loss falls predictably as a power law in params/data/compute, which is why "same block, more of it" has been the dominant strategy.

slides.title: Pre-norm vs post-norm, one more time
slides.body: Post-norm (original) needs LR warmup and is finicky past ~12 layers; pre-norm trains stably at 100+ layers because the residual identity path is never normalized. This single placement choice is *why* the block stacks to GPT-3 depth at all — it ties together everything you learned in the LayerNorm and residual lessons.

question.question: Why use 96 blocks rather than a few very wide blocks at the same parameter count?
options: Depth lets the model compose many rounds of attention+FFN; a 1-block net at the same params can only do one round
Fewer blocks would be faster but always less accurate by a fixed amount
It's arbitrary with no capability impact
question.explanation: Depth buys *composition*: each block's output feeds the next, enabling multi-step computation. The same parameters in one enormous block can only do a single round of mixing+transform. Scaling laws tune the exact depth:width ratio, but qualitatively, depth is what enables staged reasoning.

question.question: Diagnose the blow-up.
question.scenario: You 'simplified' the block by dropping its LayerNorms (keeping residual + attention + FFN), then stacked it 24×. Activations explode/NaN after a few layers, even with LR tuning.

rubricCriteria.description: residual additions accumulate activation magnitude every layer
with no normalization the scale grows unbounded across 24 blocks → overflow/NaN
fix: restore pre-norm LayerNorm inside each sublayer to bound per-token scale

question.explanation: Residual streams accumulate scale with depth; LayerNorm is what re-bounds it each layer. Remove LN and depth makes activations diverge.

hints: What do residual additions do to activation scale over depth?
Which component re-bounds per-token scale each layer?
slides.workedSolution: Each residual add increases activation magnitude; over 24 layers, with no LN, the scale grows unbounded → overflow. Pre-norm LN inside each sublayer renormalizes per token every layer, restoring stability.

question.question: A residual+attention+FFN block with NO LayerNorm blows up when stacked 24×. Best fix?
options: Add pre-norm LayerNorm inside each sublayer to keep per-token activation scale bounded across depth
question.explanation: Residual adds compound magnitude every layer; LN renormalizes each token per layer so the deep stack stays numerically stable.

slides.title: Part 5 — You can now read any transformer

question.prompt: Explain a transformer block to your pet: its two sublayers, the wrapping, and why blocks stack.

rubricCriteria.description: attention + position-wise FFN are the two sublayers
each is wrapped in LayerNorm (inside) + a residual connection (around)
the residual stream lets many blocks stack without the signal vanishing

slides.title: You can now read any transformer
slides.body: Tokens → embeddings → [attention + FFN, each wrapped in LayerNorm + residual] × N → softmax head. Every variant you'll meet (GPT, Llama, ViT) is a tweak on this skeleton — RoPE here, SwiGLU there, GQA for serving. You've built the whole thing from first principles.
